# Slurp

> A lightweight, agent-first templating engine. You write pages, components and
> layouts; it compiles them to plain HTML with almost no client JavaScript.
> Sections and blocks additionally declare a typed schema, so a non-technical
> person can edit a page through a form without touching the template. The
> mental model closest to it is a small Astro.

Version 0.1.0, pre-1.0. The language and the API will change without a
deprecation cycle until 1.0.

Everything below was verified against the compiler, mostly by rendering the
construct and recording the result. `llms-full.txt` is the complete reference
and is GENERATED from the same data an MCP server serves at run time, so the two
cannot drift. That is enforced, not merely intended: CI regenerates the file and
fails if it differs from what is committed.

## Read this first if you are writing a template

There is an MCP server, `@slurp/mcp`, that runs the real compiler in-process. It
gives you `slurp_validate` (structured diagnostics including the security walk),
`slurp_render` (HTML plus development-mode warnings), `slurp_lint` (the silent
failures the compiler does not report), `slurp_schema` and `slurp_reference`.
Use it if you can: it closes the correction loop in one call.

Without it, read `llms-full.txt` and pay particular attention to the gotchas
below, because most Slurp mistakes are SILENT. The language is deliberately
total and tolerant: missing data renders the empty string, budgets truncate
rather than abort, and unknown editor settings are dropped rather than rejected.
That is what makes it safe to render an untrusted template in a shared service,
and it is also why a mistake tends to produce a plausible-looking page rather
than an error.

## A complete file

```slurp
---
using "@components/ProductCard"
section {
  name: "Featured"
  settings {
    heading: text = "Featured products"
    limit:   number = 8 { min: 1, max: 24 }
  }
}
---
<section>
  <h2>${ section.settings.heading }</h2>
  {each product, i in products | limit(8) | sort("price")}
    <ProductCard product={product} featured={loop.first} />
  {empty}
    <p>Nothing here yet.</p>
  {/each}
</section>
```

## Syntax surface, complete

- Interpolation: `${ expr }`, always HTML-escaped. `{ expr }` is the same thing.
- Raw output: `{html expr}`, or `{html expr sanitize}` for untrusted input. This
  is the only way to bypass escaping.
- Comments: `{* stripped from the output *}`.
- Block tags, all of them: `{if}` `{else if}` `{else}`, `{each}` `{empty}`,
  `{match}`, `{fetch}` `{loading}` `{error}` `{empty}`, `{repeat}`, `{try}`
  `{error}`, `{slot}`, `{layout}`, `{head}`, `{sections}`, `{blocks}`,
  `{$let}`, `{debug}`, `{redirect}`, `{next}`.
  There is NO `{with}` and no `{case}`.
- Frontmatter, between `---` lines: `using`, `using type`, `type`, `props`,
  `middleware`, `section { }`, `block { }`. There is NO `layout` directive.
- Value filters, 13: `upper lower currency truncate fixed date default plural
  int float js json unsafe_js`.
- Loop filters, 4, usable ONLY in an `{each}` header: `limit sort reverse
  filter`. The two tables are disjoint.
- Operators: `+ - * / % == != < > <= >= && || ! ?:` and the `|` filter pipe.
  There is no `===`, `!==`, `??`, `?.`, `in`, `**`, no bitwise operator, no
  assignment, and no arrow function.
- Setting kinds in a schema, 9: `text richtext color image icon link select
  number toggle`.

## The gotchas, in the order they bite

1. **A quoted COMPONENT prop is a literal string. A quoted ELEMENT attribute
   interpolates.** This asymmetry is the most common mistake in the language and
   nothing reports it.
   `<Card title="Hi ${name}" />` passes the characters through verbatim;
   `<Card title={`Hi ${name}`} />` is what you meant;
   `<span data-x="Hi ${name}">` was already correct.
2. **A `${ }` in a `<script>` body must end in `| js` or `| json`.** A script
   body is raw text, so HTML entity escaping is inert there. `| js` escapes for
   inside a string literal you wrote and adds no quotes; `| json` emits a
   complete self-delimiting literal. This one IS a hard compile error.
3. **A JavaScript template literal in an attribute gets eaten.** Slurp
   interpolates `${ }` in attribute values itself, against the SERVER context, so
   a client-side variable renders empty with no other sign.
   `<a :href="`/p/${item.slug}`">` is wrong; `<a :href="'/p/' + item.slug">` is
   right. Reported as a warning, not an error.
4. **In JavaScript statement position, `| js` is an ERROR.** `| js` claims the
   slot is inside a quoted string, and a declared slot is emitted verbatim.
   `@click="add(${ id | js })"` is refused; use `| json`, or quote the slot.
5. **Filter arguments must be LITERALS.** A variable argument is read as the
   empty string, so the filter falls back to its default. `currency(cur)`
   renders a leading space and NO currency symbol. `default` is the sole
   exception: its argument is evaluated in scope.
6. **`| date` parses ISO strings, not epoch milliseconds.** Fewer than three
   dash-separated parts and the input is returned UNCHANGED, so epoch millis
   render verbatim. There are no time tokens at all.
7. **Money arrives as a STRING.** A server decimal serialises as `"49.990000"`,
   so calling `.toFixed` on it in emitted JavaScript throws. Coerce first.
8. **A nested `"` inside `${ }` ends the attribute.** `<div title="${ a["k"] }">`
   truncates at the inner quote. Use `title={ a["k"] }` or single quotes inside.
9. **There are NO callable functions.** `Math.max(a, b)` parses and evaluates to
   null, silently. There are no array properties either, so `items.length` is
   null.
10. **Components and layouts get their own root scope.** They see page globals
    overlaid by their explicit props, with props winning. They do NOT see the
    caller's local bindings, so an `{each}` loop variable is invisible inside a
    component unless passed as a prop.
11. **An unresolvable component renders a placeholder, not an error.** A typo in
    an import path produces a clean build with a missing card.
12. **`{$let}` creates no template binding.** It seeds client state and emits
    only a JSON payload, so reading the name back renders empty.
13. **A loop over 1000 items loses its tail and the build still exits 0.** The
    warning is recorded in every mode, but `slurp build` prints it only with `-v`.
14. **Arithmetic coerces, comparisons do not.** `"a" + 1` is `"a1"` and `1 / 0`
    is `0`, but `"10" > 9` is FALSE and `1 == "1"` is false. Coerce with `| int`.
15. **Unknown frontmatter statements are silently skipped.** A misspelled
    directive produces no diagnostic.

## Files

- [llms-full.txt](https://github.com/bytesell/slurp/blob/main/llms-full.txt):
  the complete reference. Tags, expressions, filters, components, script rules,
  frontmatter, schemas, every error code and every limit.
- [README.md](https://github.com/bytesell/slurp/blob/main/README.md): install,
  the CLI, and the known gaps in 0.1.0.
- [SLURP_DOCS.md](https://github.com/bytesell/slurp/blob/main/SLURP_DOCS.md):
  the long-form language documentation.
- [docs/security-model.md](https://github.com/bytesell/slurp/blob/main/docs/security-model.md):
  where the default escaping is and is not sufficient. Read before using `{html}`.
- [mcp/README.md](https://github.com/bytesell/slurp/blob/main/mcp/README.md):
  the MCP server, and how to register it with a coding agent.
